title: A city frozen in ash
text: When Vesuvius erupted in AD 79, it destroyed Pompeii in a day and accidentally {{1}} it for the ages. A column of ash and pumice rose above the bay, and the wind carried the fall-out {{2}} onto the city, burying it under six metres of debris. The people who lingered — and many did, returning to rescue belongings — were killed by later surges of hot gas, their bodies leaving {{3}} in the hardened ash that nineteenth-century archaeologists learned to fill with plaster. The result is a city frozen mid-habit: loaves still in the oven, election slogans on the walls, a dog {{4}} against its chain, medical instruments laid out for surgery. Pompeii transformed how we see the ancient world. Written sources {{5}} describe elites and emperors; here are the offices, snack bars, graffiti and laundry businesses of ordinary life, in unprecedented {{6}}. The site has suffered from weather, tourism and wartime bombing, and modern conservation is a race against {{7}}. New scanning techniques now {{8}} archaeologists to excavate with a light touch, unearthing rooms without cutting into them. The volcano, having taken the city, turned out to be its most careful archivist.

gaps.explanation: 'accidentally preserved it for the ages' — kept it undamaged; prevail = win out, and 'prevailed it' is not grammatical.
'carried the fall-out directly onto the city' — straight onto it; distinctly = clearly, dominantly = in a ruling manner.
'bodies leaving cavities in the hardened ash' — small hollows; cavern = a large cave, which is the wrong scale.
'a dog straining against its chain' — pulling hard to get free; stroll = walk leisurely, strop = sharpen a blade.
'Written sources mostly describe elites' — mainly; merely = only, which falsely claims they describe nothing else.
'ordinary life in unprecedented detail' — with a level of precision never seen; dispute = disagreement, disorder = mess.
'a race against time' — the fixed idiom for hurrying before it is too late; no article is used, which fits 'time' alone.
'techniques now allow archaeologists to excavate' — let them; afford takes a noun ('can afford it'), allot = assign, adhere takes 'to'.
